problem: The sentence 'the normal derivative of V jumps by σ/ε₀' hides a sign. Taking the normal n to point from side 1 to side 2, the field jump is E₂ₙ − E₁ₙ = σ/ε₀, and because Eₙ = −∂V/∂n the potential derivative obeys ∂V/∂n|₁ − ∂V/∂n|₂ = σ/ε₀, i.e. ∂V/∂n|₂ − ∂V/∂n|₁ = −σ/ε₀. A student reading 'jumps by σ/ε₀' will very likely write the jump with the wrong sign.
fix: State the direction and the sign: with n pointing from side 1 to side 2, ∂V/∂n|₂ − ∂V/∂n|₁ = −σ/ε₀ (magnitude σ/ε₀), which is the same statement as E₂ₙ − E₁ₙ = σ/ε₀.
